description: Massive (formerly Polygon.io) financial news: ticker-tagged US stock market headlines with publisher, article URL, image, summary, and per-ticker sentiment insights. Use for "what is the news on $TICKER" or "market-moving headlines today". Company-keyed: pass `ticker` or `cik`. Massive tags every company an article mentions, so each item carries `subject`: "primary" (the company is the article's subject: named in the headline, or the only/lead tagged ticker) or "mention" (tagged, but the article is about something else, e.g. an ETF or a rival); `primary_only: true` drops the mentions. Page with `cursor`: pass the `next_cursor` of the previous response. Prefer over web search for equity-focused news. Without a key of your own this runs on Pipeworx's shared free Massive key (5 requests per minute across every caller, so it can throttle): pass your own Massive key as `_apiKey` (free at massive.com/dashboard/keys) and the call uses it instead, with a private limit. Micro-cap coverage is thin: for a very small company, country_news and bing_news_search often hold more recent headlines, and a throttled call's error names them with arguments filled from yours.

_apiKey.description: Optional. Your own Massive (formerly Polygon.io) API key. Omit it and the call uses Pipeworx's shared free key (5 requests per minute across all callers); pass yours and it is used instead, for a private limit. Free key at massive.com/dashboard/keys. Never echoed back or cached.

cik.description: SEC CIK (digits), resolved to a ticker through SEC when `ticker` is not given.

cursor.description: Opaque paging cursor: the `next_cursor` of the previous response. It carries the original filters.

primary_only.description: Return only items where the company is the primary subject (applied to the fetched page, so a page can come back short; keep paging).
